subject: SLO qualification: dedicated capacity — HealthLytics next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara.singh@healthlytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: HealthLytics SLO qualification — summary + asks

Thanks for the time today, team — quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope the Dedicated pilot. High-level asks from HealthLytics: p95 text-gen latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), sustained throughput ~120 requests/sec during peak windows, and streaming support for long responses (tail p99 < 800ms). They expect ~200 concurrent users with ~1.5 requests/minute per user at peak.

Notes from the call:
- Primary model: open-llama-70B-ish variant (they want to test a 70B and a 13B quantized option)
- Workload shape: mix 60% short-complete (<=128 tokens), 40% streaming long (300-600 tokens)
- SLA ask: monthly uptime + latency SLOs for Dedicated with clear fallbacks to 13B variant if resource constrained

Immediate asks for Redwood engineering ops: 
1) Provide recommended GPU SKU shortlist with expected reserved throughput (tokens/s or requests/s) and rough cost delta (A100-40GB vs H100-80GB vs L4-80GB quantized paths). Please include guidance for streaming tails and KV-cache impact.
2) Produce an SLO acceptance matrix we can share with HealthLytics that maps their targets to test cases (p95/p99 latencies, concurrency windows, batching knobs).
3) Confirm timeline for a 1-week pilot (bench + smoke) and required artifacts from the customer (sample prompts, token distribution, service account with test keys).

Deliverables: Ben — GPU shortlist + microbenchmark summary by Tue 2026-09-06. Karthik — SLO acceptance matrix template and pilot runbook by Wed 2026-09-07. I'll host a 30-min alignment on Thu AM PT if those are ready.

- Sofia
Product & Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Follow-up: HealthLytics SLO qualification — summary + asks

Adding my bench notes and preliminary SKU recommendations — high level first, detailed PDF attached. Short summary:

1) H100-80GB (fp16)
- Strengths: best single-instance throughput for 70B fp16; streaming tail latency good when combined with our continuous-batching engine and KV cache warm-up.
- Reserved throughput estimate: ~80-120 requests/sec for short prompts at p95 < 250ms with concurrency target ~200 (using a 4-node dedicated pool + batching).
- Cost: highest; recommended only if HealthLytics requires 70B fp16 fidelity.

2) A100-40GB (int8 / quantized 4-bit)
- Strengths: solid cost/perf for 70B quantized or native 13B. Lower memory means more model shards and slightly higher cross-node comms—small hit to streaming tail.
- Reserved throughput estimate: ~45-70 requests/sec per node for short prompts; plan for 6-8 nodes to hit 120 rps with buffer.
- Cost: mid; good middle ground if they accept quantized tradeoffs.

3) L4-80GB or similar inference-focused SKU (8-bit quantized flows)
- Strengths: best unit economics on quantized 13B. Streaming tails typically lower variance due to fewer NVLink hops (single-node serving of small models).
- Reserved throughput estimate: 120+ rps for 13B quant at p95 well under 250ms with 3-4 nodes; for 70B quantized, expect higher latency and lower throughput.
- Cost: best for cost-constrained pilots.

Bench caveats and asks:
- Need their representative prompt set, token-length distribution, and any safety/eval hooks that add extra compute.
- For streaming tails, KV-cache warm-up time and prefix reuse matter — include a 'prefix reuse' test in the pilot.
- I'll attach gpu_microbenchmarks-summary.pdf with our 70B/13B runs (simulated public workload) and an appendix mapping batch sizes to p95/p99.

Next steps: I'll upload the PDF to the Drive link and share a short runbook snippet in HubSpot. Sofia — Ben can take the lead on the GPU shortlist deliverable.

— Ben
Solutions Engineering

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: HealthLytics SLO qualification — summary + asks

Thanks — added a compact SLO acceptance matrix draft inline below. I took the call notes and mapped them to practical pass/fail checks for the pilot. Please iterate.

SLO acceptance matrix (draft):
- Test A: Short prompt p95
  - Input: 128 tokens request mix (30k samples)
  - Pass: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms
  - Observability: token-level latency breakdown, route-level traces

- Test B: Streaming long response tail
  - Input: 400 token outputs, 40% of traffic simulated as streaming
  - Pass: tail p99 (end-to-end) < 800ms after first byte
  - Observability: per-chunk latency, retransmit/fallback counts

- Test C: Sustained throughput window
  - Input: 120 req/sec sustained for 10 minutes with realistic concurrency pattern (200 users)
  - Pass: no dropped requests, avg CPU/GPU util <= 85% (headroom for spikes)

- Test D: Failover and rollback
  - Input: Simulate node OOM / preemption -> automatic fallback to quantized 13B
  - Pass: client-visible error rate < 0.5% during transition; latency spike < 2x baseline for < 60s

Pilot runbook bullets:
- Pre-pilot: customer provides prompt set + service account + expected daily peak window (we got Tue 9–10AM PT)
- Pilot: 3-day microbench (bench + streaming validation) + 4-day soak (production-like traffic)
- Post-pilot: extract metrics, produce acceptance report and runbook recommendations

I'll formalize this into the slo_acceptance_matrix.xlsx and the HubSpot record by 2026-09-07. Sofia — can you confirm the Thu AM sync window? Also tagging Ben to validate the node counts in his estimates for the sustained window.

- Karthik
Performance & Infrastructure

Appreciate the quick turnaround, everyone. Confirming next steps from our side:
- We'll export a 48-hour representative prompt sample and token distribution by EOD Mon (attach: sample_prompts.json)
- We can provide a service account for the pilot and a small sandbox dataset for safety checks
- Pilot timing: We prefer Thu 2026-09-09 for the alignment call and can start the bench on Fri 2026-09-10 if that works for Redwood.

A couple of clarifying Qs:
1) For the fallback behavior — will the client see a different model id in the response header when we switch to 13B? We want transparent telemetry.
2) For the streaming tail measurement — do you measure p99 from first byte or last byte? We prefer first byte to capture perceived latency.

Ben — thank you for the SKU breakdown. We'll review the PDF and give a cost sensitivity (H100 vs A100) note back with the sample prompts.

Thanks — Tara
